To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the critical strain energy release rates, G lc, of alumia trihydrate (ATH), calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ), and glass bead (GB) filled epoxy resin were determined as a function filler volume fraction, and that G lc showed a maxima at a filler volume fractions of approximately 0,18 for ATH and GB and at 0.25 for CaCO3.

the fracture toughness increases with the volume fraction of alumina tri-hydrate particles, but the strain energy release rate shows a peak at an intermediate volume fraction, and that the breakaway parameter is approximately 2.0 for the alumina tri-hyd-rate particles.

the critical strain energy release rates, G lc, of alumna trihydrate (ATH)-filled epoxy resin showed a maximum at filler volume fraction of about 18%, and the fracture toughness, K ic, increased linearly up with volume fraction of filler up to 55%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of particle strength, filler volume fraction and particle size on the toughening of brittle epoxy resin.
the fracture toughness of alumina tri-hydrate filled polyepoxy resin and the toughening mechanism.
the role of particle strength in the fracture of filled polymers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
crack pinning and crack blunting are important toughening mechanisms in the intermediate volume fractions, while particle fracture is important at high volume fractions.
the fracture behaviour of the ATH filled resin is a function of both the filler volume fraction and particle size, with a strong dependence on particle strength.
the fracture toughness of the filled epoxy resin is a complex function of filler volume and particle strength.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the critical strain energy release rates and critical stress intensity factors for alumina trihydrate filled epoxies are determined by the particle strength, the filler volume fraction and the particle size.
the fracture behaviour of the epoxy resin is strongly dependent on the volume fraction and particle strength of the filler.
the fracture toughness of the epoxy resin increases with filler volume fraction, but that the increase is not linear.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the critical energy release rate and fracture toughness of a filled resin can be predicted from the particle strength and filler content, and that the fracture toughness of filled resin systems can be increased by using strong filler particles.
the strength of the filler is a key factor in determining its ability to toughen the resin matrix.
particle strength is an important parameter for determining the fracture toughness of a filled polymer system.
